```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(zoo)
library(arrow)
library(scales)
library(lubridate)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggbeeswarm)

# ==========================================
# GOOGLE TRENDS DATA PREP
# ==========================================
all_df <- read_csv("data/clean/clean_time_series_US_6.csv")

# Convert to tidy format and rename
tidy_df <- all_df |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(matcha, chai, cold_brew, mocha, refresher, psl, smoothie),
    names_to = "keyword",
    values_to = "interest"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    keyword = recode(
      keyword,
      matcha = "Matcha",
      chai = "Chai",
      cold_brew = "Cold Brew",
      mocha = "Mocha",
      refresher = "Refresher",
      psl = "Pumpkin Spice Latte",
      smoothie = "Smoothie"
    )
  )

# Rolling 12-month average growth stat (2021 vs 2026)
growth_stats <- tidy_df |>
  arrange(keyword, time) |>
  group_by(keyword) |>

  # Get the yearly average for first and last year
  summarise(
    first_year = mean(head(interest, 12), na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year = mean(tail(interest, 12), nam.rm = TRUE)
  ,
    pct_growth = if_else(
      first_year > 0,
        ((last_year - first_year) / first_year) * 100,
        NA_real_
    ),
  ) |>
  
  # Arrange in descending order 
  arrange(desc(pct_growth))


# Growth stability matrix info
matrix_info <- tidy_df |>
  group_by(keyword) |>
  summarise(
    volatility = sd(interest, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(interest, na.rm = TRUE),
    first_year_avg = mean(head(interest, 12), na.rm = TRUE),
    last_year_avg = mean(tail(interest, 12), na.rm = TRUE),
    growth_rate = (last_year_avg - first_year_avg) / first_year_avg,
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

median_growth <- median(matrix_info$growth_rate, na.rm = TRUE)
median_volatility <- median(matrix_info$volatility, na.rm = TRUE)

# Monthly Seasonality Dataframe
monthly_avg <- tidy_df |>
  mutate(month = month(time, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)) |>
  group_by(keyword, month) |>
  summarise(avg_interest = mean(interest, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# Filter for recent trends (for Rolling Average plot)
trends_recent <- tidy_df |>
  filter(time >= as.Date("2016-01-01"))

# Rolling Average Dataframe
rol_avg <- trends_recent |>
  group_by(keyword) |>
  arrange(time) |>
  mutate(rolling_avg = rollmean(interest, k = 6, fill = NA))

# ==========================================
# TIKTOK DATA PREP
# ==========================================
tagged_data <- read_parquet("data/clean/clean_tiktok_data_tagged.parquet")

tag_counts <- tagged_data |>
  summarise(
    Starbucks = sum(commercial),
    `Ceremonial/Traditional` = sum(traditional),
    `Flavors` = sum(flavor_innovation),
    `Standard Matcha` = sum(cafe_beverage)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    everything(),
    names_to = "category",
    values_to = "count"
  ) |>
  # Calculate frequency percentage 
  mutate(percentage = count / sum(count))

engagement_rates <- tagged_data |>
  select(
    engagement_rate,
    commercial,
    traditional,
    flavor_innovation,
    cafe_beverage
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      commercial,
      traditional,
      flavor_innovation,
      cafe_beverage
    ),
    names_to = "theme",
    values_to = "present"
  ) |>
  filter(present) |>
  mutate(
    theme = recode(
      theme,
      commercial = "Starbucks",
      traditional = "Ceremonial/Traditional",
      flavor_innovation = "Flavors",
      cafe_beverage = "Standard Matcha"
    )
  )

paired_stats <- tagged_data |>
  summarise(
    commercial_total = sum(commercial, na.rm = TRUE),
    overlap1 = sum(commercial & flavor_innovation, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    pct_overlap1 = overlap1 / commercial_total * 100
  )

powder_stat <- engagement_rates |>
  group_by(theme) |>
  summarise(med_eng = median(engagement_rate, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(theme %in% c("Ceremonial/Traditional", "Starbucks")) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = theme, values_from = med_eng) |>
  mutate(multiplier = `Ceremonial/Traditional` / Starbucks) |>
  pull(multiplier)
```

## Column {width="40%"}

### Growth Stability Matrix
```{r}
target_growth <- 1.0
high_vol <- 0.75

ggplot(matrix_info, aes(x = growth_rate, y = volatility, label = keyword)) +
  # Quadrant Lines
  geom_hline(yintercept = high_vol, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7, color = "gray45") +
  annotate("text", x = target_growth + 1.25, y = high_vol + 0.08, label = "High volatility \nconsidered at 75%", size = 3, color = "gray30") + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = target_growth, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7, color = "gray45") + 
  annotate("text", x = target_growth + 0.17, y = high_vol + 0.68, label = "Target growth \nset at 100%", size = 3, color = "gray30") +
  
  geom_point(size = 5, color = "#0077BB", alpha = 1) +
  geom_text_repel(
    # Conditional statement to set Matcha label to bold
    aes(fontface = ifelse(keyword == "Matcha", "bold", "plain")), 
    size = 4.5, 
    point.padding = 0.45, 
    box.padding = 1.2, 
    min.segment.length = 0) + 
  
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, 2.5)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1.5)) +
  
  labs(
    title = "Growth-Stability of Beverages",
    subtitle = "Comparing rolling 12-month volume averages against volatility",
    x = "Long-Term Growth Rate (Trailing 12-Months vs. Baseline)",
    y = "Volatility (Coefficient of Variation)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16), 
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), 
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90"),
    
  )
```

### Content Theme Frequency on TikTok
```{r}
ggplot(tag_counts, aes(x = reorder(category, -percentage), y = percentage, fill = category)) + 
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "turbo", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent()) +
  labs(
    title = "Content Theme Frequency on TikTok",
    subtitle = "Frequency of common matcha content themes across videos ",
    x = "Content Theme",
    y = "Percentage of Videos"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12)
  ) + 
  geom_text(
    aes(label = percent(percentage, accuracy = 1)),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 4, 
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "gray30"
  )
```

### Engagement Rate by Category Beeswarm Plot
```{r}
ggplot(engagement_rates, aes(x = reorder(theme, engagement_rate, FUN = median), y = engagement_rate, color = theme)) + 
  geom_quasirandom(alpha = 0.6, size = 2.5, width = 0.2) + 
  # Black point to show median
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "point", shape = 15, size = 3, color = "black") +
  scale_color_viridis_d(option = "turbo", begin = 0.2, end = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = label_percent()) + 
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 0.3)) + 
  labs(
    title = "Engagement Rate Distribution by Matcha Content Themes",
    subtitle = "Videos may belong to multiple themes. Black square indicates the median engagement rate. \nSample size varies per theme. \nEngagement is calculated by (Likes+Comments+Shares+Saves / Views)",
    x = "Content Theme",
    y = "Engagement Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12)
  )
```


# Data & Additional Info

This dashboard integrates Google Trends search data with TikTok engagement data to examine matcha as a consumer beverage, combining macro-level demand signals with social media content behavior.

**Google Trends Data** 

Google Trends time-series data was collected for multiple beverage-related keywords: chai, cold brew, matcha, mocha, pumpkin spice latte, refresher, and smoothie. The dataset spans from June of 2021 to May of 2026 on a monthly resolution for the United States.

**TikTok Data**

TikTok data was collected using the Apify API based on matcha-related hashtags. The final dataset contains approximately 520 videos. Each record includes engagement metrics such as views, likes, comments, shares, and saves.

**Theme Tagging System**

To analyze content structure, videos were tagged using rule-based keyword detection applied to captions. These tags are not mutually exclusive, and a single video may belong to multiple tags.

**Matrix Volatility Threshold**

Volatility in the Growth-Stability Matrix is calculated using the Coefficient of Variation (COV) to normalize variance across different market sizes. The 75% (0.75) high-volatility threshold was selected as a business heuristic to isolate highly erratic, seasonal fads (e.g., Pumpkin Spice Latte) from stable, year-round consumer staples. While a standard metric flags COV > 1.0 as extreme and unstable, consumer search trends carry inherently more noise, making 0.75 a stricter test for stability.
